main_text.l: les & refractarios homines, qui in Testamen-ti noui inciderunt tempora, & Deum profitentur se scire, sed factis negant, quum sint abominandi & rebelles, & ad omne opus bonum reprobi. Tit.1.16. Porrò, si qui agnoscunt πανα-ρμονέαν[?] quandam esse diuinorum Attributorum, quæ certè τῷ λόγῳ solùm, non autem τῷ εἶναι, inter se distingui debent: illi facilè dabunt, unum & eundem Jehouám, mundi gubernatorem moderatissimum, præmia & pœnas sapienter dispensantè, & summè iustum esse, & eundem summè misericordem esse καὶ φιλανθρωπος.

Secundò, Si nobis in Domino persuasum est, Jesum Christum heri & hodie eundem & in secula esse, Heb.13.8: Agnum esse mactatum iam inde à iactis fundamentis mundi (si inquam precium, ἐνέργειαν[?] & applicationem meritorum eius, species) Apoc.13.8. nec deniq; sine hoc sequestro, Ecclesiam ullo tempore esse potuisse: non equidem, vel dubiū vel obscurum erit, ista Pauli verba: At nunc (noster ille Pontifex eo) ex excellentius ministerium sortitus est, quo præstantioris est fœderis intercessor, quod præstantioribus promissis sanctum est, Heb.8.6. nequaquam hoc ἁπλῶς, simpliciter, affirmare, Christum Do

page.notes: The Greek words are printed in Greek letters and are copied as they appear; accents on the first Greek words are doubtful. "πανα-ρμονέαν" is uncertain, as is "ἐνέργειαν". The line "summè iustum" has a line-break hyphen after "sum-" and the words run together in the print. "ex cellentius" is printed with a gap and is read as "excellentius". Running head "VNICO" read as "UNICO" by the vowel rule. Catchword "minum" is the start of the next page's word "Dominum". The Hebrew and Greek labels are copied as printed.
